papers.title: Influence of Selected Heat Treatment on Alloy Properties of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: Titanium is the polymorphic metal whose recrystallization temperature significantly affects its final properties. The area between 850 C and 995 C is a very important area from the point of view of heat treatment of titanium alloys. It is a transition area just below the β transition limit. This article deals with the analysis of the influence of thermal loading on the change in tensile strength and fracture behavior of titanium alloys in comparison with thermally unloaded samples. Monitoring of fracture surfaces and description of the internal structure of the material.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理，而是研究传统铸造/锻造合金的热处理对拉伸性能的影响，与本方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not specify additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it investigates heat treatment effects on conventionally processed alloy, lacking the AM-specific post-processing context required.

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to understand how selected heat treatments affect the tensile properties and fracture behavior of Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V specimens were subjected to specific thermal loading regimes and subsequently evaluated via tensile testing and fracture surface analysis.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment altered the tensile strength and fracture characteristics of the alloy compared to untreated samples.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through mechanical tensile tests and microscopic examination of fracture surfaces.
